records.title: Critical Media Literacy
records.header: TCOM 101 Critical Media Literacy (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 101 Critical Media Literacy (5) SSc Surveys historical, economic, and cultural contexts for contemporary media to foster critical literacy from local and global perspectives. Evaluates media messages to understand power structures and tools of persuasion in film, television, journalism, interactive and social media, sports media, and youth media. Course overlaps with: BIS 235.

records.title: Media and Society
records.header: TCOM 201 Media and Society (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 201 Media and Society (5) SSc Explores theoretical perspectives and core issues in the relationship between the media and society, including the production and reception of both news and entertainment. Evaluates the historical, cultural, political and economic contexts of media industries, representations, and audiences.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Social Media
records.header: TCOM 220 Social Media (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 220 Social Media (5) SSc Explores the evolving world of social media and assesses their social, cultural, and political meanings and implications. Develops skills to critically reflect on social media experiences and develop effective media strategies as communication professionals.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence: Media, Culture, and Power
records.header: TCOM 221 Artificial Intelligence: Media, Culture, and Power (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 221 Artificial Intelligence: Media, Culture, and Power (5) A&H Explores how artificial intelligence fits into the overall study of modern media, including disruptions to the current media landscape. Through a critical perspective, the course examines key ways that machine learning, and our uses of it, may ultimately challenge - or uphold - structures of social power and privilege. Students will consider the implications of AI, including its perils and promises, for us, our society, and the world around us.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Media Globalization and Citizenship
records.header: TCOM 230 Media Globalization and Citizenship (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 230 Media Globalization and Citizenship (5) SSc Introduces key concepts in international communication and global media studies such as cultural imperialism, electronic colonialism, and media globalization. Through case studies from around the world, students evaluate their positions as global citizens and explore opportunities for activism.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Television Studies
records.header: TCOM 247 Television Studies (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 247 Television Studies (5) SSc Introduces the study of television as a social, cultural, and political force. Examines the production, distribution, and reception of television texts of different genres, including news and entertainment; evaluates how television reflects and influences different societies and groups; explores television in different historical periods and through various technologies. Course overlaps with: CMS 274.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Media for Social Justice
records.header: TCOM 250 Media for Social Justice (5) SSc/A&H
records.text: TCOM 250 Media for Social Justice (5) SSc/A&H Examines how media and information and communication technologies are used as tools to challenge inequality and advance social justice goals. It introduces frameworks, concepts, local and global case studies to understand how social, cultural, political, economic, and personal factors may hinder or advance social change. Students learn to produce a storytelling project demonstrating their knowledge of concepts and ideas explored in the course.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Communication History
records.header: TCOM 254 Communication History (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 254 Communication History (5) SSc Addresses the complexities of media and communication historically, particularly the technologies and their impact on society. Includes development of different forms of communication and the intertwining of the history of mass communication with the history of other social institutions.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Ethical Issues in Mass Communication
records.header: TCOM 257 Ethical Issues in Mass Communication (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: TCOM 257 Ethical Issues in Mass Communication (5) A&H/SSc Focuses on different types of media producers - in journalism, popular culture, and digital media - as a link between the mass media and society. Through a study of ethical theories, evaluates the ethical dilemmas of contemporary media producers and their audiences from a critical media studies framework.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Children and Media
records.header: TCOM 258 Children and Media (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 258 Children and Media (5) SSc Examines the historical, sociological, and psychological context of children consuming myriad forms of media. Brings together scholarship from child psychology, television criticism, and reception studies.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Writing, Reporting, and Editing for the Mass Media
records.header: TCOM 275 Writing, Reporting, and Editing for the Mass Media (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 275 Writing, Reporting, and Editing for the Mass Media (5) A&H Introduces students to writing, reporting, and editing for web, print and television. Focuses on developing a concise writing style, passion for thorough, accurate reporting, and a sensitivity to various audiences' needs and interests. Emphasizes information gathering and interviewing skills. Explores professional norms and expectations with introduction to paths for obtaining media-related internships and careers.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Environmental Communication: Media, Resistance, and Power
records.header: TCOM 310 Environmental Communication: Media, Resistance, and Power (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 310 Environmental Communication: Media, Resistance, and Power (5) SSc Explores how media shape our understanding of environmental issues and disasters - from wildfires to corporate greenwashing. Students analyze how ownership structures influence environmental narratives across media platforms, including social media, while examining how alternative voices challenge mainstream coverage.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Ecology, Inequality, and Popular Culture
records.header: TCOM 312 Ecology, Inequality, and Popular Culture (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: TCOM 312 Ecology, Inequality, and Popular Culture (5) SSc, DIV Surveys the debates within cultural/critical studies to explore how portrayals of ecology in popular culture directly relate to representations of gender, sexuality, nationality, ethnicity, and class. Applies numerous critical perspectives to understand key power structures in film, television, magazines, and novels from the U.S. and international sources.

records.title: Principles of Web Design
records.header: TCOM 320 Principles of Web Design (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 320 Principles of Web Design (5) A&H Examines the theories and techniques of visual and design rhetoric to web design. Discusses how purpose, audience, and context affect the development of web pages and other electronic documents. Explores principles of web-based design, creation, layout, editing, publishing, and maintenance through web design practices.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Mobile Communication and Social Practice
records.header: TCOM 330 Mobile Communication and Social Practice (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 330 Mobile Communication and Social Practice (5) SSc Explores social practices surrounding mobile communication technologies and identifies their social, cultural, and political consequences across the globe. Develops a critical understanding of the historical development of mobile technologies and related key concepts. creates design prototype of mobile apps to understand and augment everyday mobile user experience.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Global TV: Format, Genre, and Reception
records.header: TCOM 340 Global TV: Format, Genre, and Reception (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 340 Global TV: Format, Genre, and Reception (5) SSc Focuses on current issues and topics in global television studies. Explores several case studies of television format from around the world in order to understand the development and evolution of television genre such as soap opera and reality TV in a transnational context. Course overlaps with: BIS 235.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Global Music Video
records.header: TCOM 343 Global Music Video (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 343 Global Music Video (5) A&H Examines music video as an art form, cultural institution, and global media industry. Considers the history, aesthetics, and politics of music videos made around the world.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Social Media for Media Professionals
records.header: TCOM 346 Social Media for Media Professionals (5)
records.text: TCOM 346 Social Media for Media Professionals (5) Explores the use of social media in professional areas including journalism, public relations, and content production. Emphasizes specific skills including understanding/interacting with audiences; using analytics; curating story/content ideas; and developing strong writing and video production skills. Focuses on developing individual professional social media brands and introduces best practices for obtaining internships and jobs in the field.

records.title: Television Criticism and Application
records.header: TCOM 347 Television Criticism and Application (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 347 Television Criticism and Application (5) A&H Explores narrative structures and production techniques utilized in television in an integrated manner. Analyzes and discusses critical approaches to television texts and techniques, including use of camera angles, lighting design, sound effects, and editing. Explores the application of basic production to techniques in a hands-on manner. Course overlaps with: CMS 273.

records.title: Non-fiction Writing for Television
records.header: TCOM 348 Non-fiction Writing for Television (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 348 Non-fiction Writing for Television (5) A&H Explores non-fiction styles of writing for television, including news writing and documentary writing, with a focus on the development of stores from a proposal to a script. Addresses issues and conflicts that arise with the linking of visual images and spoken words in non-fiction television genres.

records.title: News Writing
records.header: TCOM 349 News Writing (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 349 News Writing (5) A&H Covers principles of news writing and reporting, including lead writing, Associated Press style conventions, news judgment, and ethical and legal issues.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Editing and Design for Print Media
records.header: TCOM 350 Editing and Design for Print Media (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 350 Editing and Design for Print Media (5) A&H Covers elements of print media editing and design including: selection and editing of news copy; headline writing; typography; selection, sizing and cropping of photos; functions of layout; principles of publication design and their practical applications. Students also complete several page design projects as teams.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Video Production
records.header: TCOM 351 Video Production (5, max. 10) A&H
records.text: TCOM 351 Video Production (5, max. 10) A&H Examines principles of visual and audio communication, including storytelling through image, movement, spoken words, and other sounds in an integrated manner. Discusses critical approaches to audio-visual production and engages hands-on practice to develop production skills. Prerequisite: TCOM 347.

records.title: Political Economy of the Media
records.header: TCOM 380 Political Economy of the Media (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 380 Political Economy of the Media (5) SSc Examines the historical evolution and economic structure in which media industries are embedded and develops theoretical and analytical tools for the evaluation of media industries. Surveys patterns of ownership and control, government policies, and other issues in media industries, including newspapers, magazines, television, motion pictures, and recorded music.

records.title: Writing for Public Relations
records.header: TCOM 387 Writing for Public Relations (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 387 Writing for Public Relations (5) A&H Explores aspects of public relations writing, including news releases for print and broadcast media, advertising copy, speeches, newsletters, and crisis communication. Emphasizes writing for clarity and interest, simplifying complex issues, and conducting effective media relations. Prerequisite: either TCOM 275 or TCOM 349.

records.title: Advanced Web Design
records.header: TCOM 420 Advanced Web Design (5) A&H
records.text: TCOM 420 Advanced Web Design (5) A&H Explores advanced concepts, practices, and techniques in large-scale, user-centered web design. Emphasizes interaction design, web usability, and accessibility; design communication and design lifecycle; content management; ongoing site management; and cross-cultural issues. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in TCOM 320.

records.title: Advertising and Consumer Culture
records.header: TCOM 440 Advertising and Consumer Culture (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 440 Advertising and Consumer Culture (5) SSc Explores the past, present, and future of advertising as a form of communication by examining television commercials, political campaigns, billboards, movie trailers, and magazine ads. Also explores the industry that creates these materials, the consumption practices they encourage, and their impact on contemporary culture.

records.title: Gender, Ethnicity, Class, and the Media
records.header: TCOM 444 Gender, Ethnicity, Class, and the Media (5) A&H/SSc, DIV
records.text: TCOM 444 Gender, Ethnicity, Class, and the Media (5) A&H/SSc, DIV Explores the media landscape as a powerful site for the construction and circulation of intersecting ideologies of privilege and difference. Studies the socio-historical origins of these ideologies, using methods of media analysis to examine their presence in numerous forms of media, including popular culture, journalism, and digital media.

records.title: Critical Approaches to Mass Communication
records.header: TCOM 453 Critical Approaches to Mass Communication (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 453 Critical Approaches to Mass Communication (5) SSc Examines how power is constructed, concentrated, and maintained through and around mass communication. Carefully evaluates the structures (patriarchy, neoliberalism, etc) that have historically served to preserve the status quo ideology in our society. Research-focused and includes application of critical theoretical frameworks.

records.title: Communications Law
records.header: TCOM 454 Communications Law (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 454 Communications Law (5) SSc Examines issues surrounding freedom of expression in the United States and citizens' and the media's legal rights in gathering and disseminating news and information. Explores the freedoms afforded by the First Amendment and shows how those protections are still evolving in the twenty-first century.

records.header: TCOM 460 Communication for Development and Social Change (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: TCOM 460 Communication for Development and Social Change (5) A&H/SSc Introduces theories and concepts associated with the origin and evolution of development communication. Examines case studies of grassroots development from Asia, Latin America and Africa to study models and practices for community participation and social change through the use of information and communication technologies.

records.title: Media and Identity in Asia
records.header: TCOM 461 Media and Identity in Asia (5) SSc
records.text: TCOM 461 Media and Identity in Asia (5) SSc Explores the dynamics of media production and consumption in Asian countries within their postcolonial and neocolonial contexts. Addresses the impact of the transnational media industry on local cultural identities, focusing on hybrid media formats and audience responses. Examines various case studies with an emphasis on regional political, economic, social, and cultural contexts.

records.text: TCOM 465 Contemporary Free Speech Issues (5) SSc Explores contemporary free speech issues in light of their social, political and economic implications in the United States. Examines United States Supreme Court cases and First Amendment theory related to those contentious free speech topics.

records.text: TCOM 470 Documentary Production and Critique (5) A&H Examines theoretical and ethical issues involved in the production of non-fiction genres while shooting and editing short-form, community-based documentaries. Prerequisite: T COM 351.

records.text: TCOM 480 Critical Media Industry Studies (5, max. 10) SSc Explores selected media industries or issues from a critical perspective. Focuses on the development of the theoretical and analytical tools to conduct critical research on media industries products and/or issues. Focus will vary, but can include the video games industry, television industry, or labor in creative industries. Recommended: TCOM 353 or TCOM 380.

Integrates the basic foundations of news gathering and writing with the skills needed to produce publishable opinion pieces. Prerequisite: either TCOM 275 or TCOM 349

records.text: TCOM 486 Feature Writing for Print and Online Media (5) A&H Explores a variety of formats for feature writing, a type of media writing that weaves together narrative with facts to entertain, educate, inform and engage audiences of various media platforms.
